parts.note: springs that gush water share a name with the author of The War of the Worlds and The Time Machine

explanation.surface: A question about an effusive author who overpraises everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gushing' seems to describe an effusive writer, but it points to sources of water that spurt up from the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: H.G. Wells was the novelist; boreholes from which water spouts carry the same name.

clue.text: Silly rhymes, whether one likes it or not

definitions.text: whether one likes it or not

explanation.surface: A comment on nonsense verse imposed on readers regardless of their taste.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a jingling, rhyming piece of nonsense, and as an idiom it means regardless of anyone's wishes.

clue.text: You will know when you've got it

definitions.text: You will know when you've got it

parts.words: You will know when you've got it
parts.note: read literally, having acquired knowledge means you then know things

explanation.surface: A reassuring promise that recognition comes the moment something is obtained.
explanation.definitionFit: Study and education give knowledge, so possessing it means you know.

explanation.surface: A question about a contract term that imposes a fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penalty clause' is a contract term, but split it: a court's punishment and a grammatical unit of words share one name.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge passes a punishment of this name, and in grammar it is a group of words containing a clause or more.

parts.note: Mary is the name of several English and Scottish queens
to land is to come ashore from a ship

explanation.surface: A monarch steps off a ship to visit a region.
explanation.walkthrough: MARYLAND is a US state on the east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Maryland is one of the fifty constituent regions of the United States.

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
SS stands for steamship, a prefix on ship names

explanation.surface: Instructions to gather everyone aboard the main vessel of a fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather together in a large body or crowd is to come together as a throng.

clue.text: What one does with a bookmaker, of course!

definitions.text: What one does with a bookmaker

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic agreement about what happens at the betting shop.
explanation.definitionFit: At a bookie's you place a wager, and the same phrase is an emphatic expression of agreement meaning certainly.

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of a titan are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A giant goes out determined to triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: To win something is to achieve or reach it through effort.

indicators.note: upset suggests the name Eddy is knocked over and its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A man called Eddy went red when he was annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating cloth with a pigment alters its hue.

parts.note: spare is read as an adjective meaning thin, not as a spare home or estate

explanation.surface: A question about owning a second house or plot of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare property' suggests surplus real estate; read 'spare' as lean or thin and 'property' as a quality.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare figure is thin, and the quality of being thin is slimness.

clue.text: One who didn't strike Shakespeare as a sword carrier

parts.note: a scab is a worker who refuses to join a strike
Shakespeare is known as the Bard (of Avon)

explanation.surface: A strikebreaker appears to be the playwright, cast as a swordsman's attendant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' looks like a blow with a sword, but it is industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath holds a blade when it is not in use.

definitions.note: taken as a noun, the act of talking

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
verse is poetry, written in lines

explanation.surface: An actor memorises a script for a speaking part.
explanation.definitionFit: Conversation, talking with others, is an old noun sense here.

explanation.surface: Politicians who are gambling.
explanation.walkthrough: Statesmen here means men from the United States. A Yankee is a British combination bet of eleven wagers on four horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans are called this informally, and in British betting the word names a multiple wager on four selections.

clue.text: No chores undone in this vessel

indicators.note: undone suggests the letters of no chores are untied and rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship where nobody does the housework.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-masted sailing ship is a kind of boat.

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study
a stance is a way of standing, a position

explanation.surface: Examining where a body of water lies.
explanation.walkthrough: Lake Constance lies between Germany, Switzerland and Austria.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Constance is the large body of water known in German as the Bodensee.

clue.text: The kind of learning that is beyond the pale

definitions.text: The kind of learning that is beyond the pale

parts.words: The kind of learning that is beyond the pale
parts.note: beyond the pale is read literally as outside the walls or boundary of a university

explanation.surface: A complaint that some education is unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beyond the pale' means unacceptable, but literally a pale is a fence: the Latin of the answer means outside the walls.
explanation.definitionFit: University courses for non-resident students are taught outside the walls, from Latin extra muros.

clue.text: Obstruction by a member may lead to dismissal

definitions.text: Obstruction by a member may lead to dismissal

parts.words: Obstruction by a member may lead to dismissal
parts.note: the member is a leg blocking the ball in cricket, not a club member

explanation.surface: A warning that a committee member who blocks business may be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is out when the ball, which would have hit the stumps, strikes the leg instead: the dismissal known as LBW.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a batter is given out if their leg stops a ball that would have hit the stumps.

clue.text: Poor tip diner provided, showing no fear

indicators.note: poor suggests tip diner is a badly made version that must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner leaves a stingy gratuity without fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fearless is bold and undaunted.

clue.text: Evidence that the deal is not perfect

definitions.text: Evidence that the deal is not perfect

parts.words: Evidence that the deal is not perfect
parts.note: deal means pine or fir timber, not a business agreement, and the flaw is a gap in the wood

explanation.surface: Proof that a business arrangement has flaws.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is softwood timber; a gap left where a knot fell out shows the plank is flawed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole in a plank where a knot has dropped out is a blemish in timber.

indicators.note: half of the two-letter word my is one letter, its second

parts.note: earnings are wages, money earned

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a bigger share of their pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Longings and cravings are strong wants.

parts.note: a.m. stands for ante meridiem, morning
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: Someone passes the time doing a morning workout.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain someone is to divert their attention pleasantly.

clue.text: A head with totally unsatisfactory delivery

parts.note: nob is a slang word for the head
all means wholly, totally

explanation.surface: Someone's head with a thoroughly poor performance.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an illegal ball, bowled with a foot over the line, is penalised with an extra run.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, an illegal ball bowled by the bowler counts as a penalty run for the batting side.

parts.note: impression is a printing of a book, not a mistaken belief

explanation.surface: A misunderstanding that has been corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impression' means a print run; the answer is a printing mistake listed with its correction.
explanation.definitionFit: A printing mistake noted in a list of corrections is a corrigendum.

clue.text: Cries from clumsy seamen on prow of boat

indicators.note: the prow is the front of a ship, so the front letter of boat

parts.note: lubbers are clumsy, unskilled sailors

explanation.surface: Awkward sailors at the front of a vessel shout out.
explanation.definitionFit: Weeps noisily, sobbing.

indicators.note: outside means the word for evil is placed around the letter for right

parts.note: bad means evil

explanation.surface: Someone hammers something wicked beyond what is proper.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, small-headed wire tack is a type of fixing pin.

explanation.surface: Stop the flow and prop things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem bleeding is to stop it, and a plant's main stalk holds up its flower.

clue.text: Gin before opening may let down an actor

parts.note: a gin is a snare for catching animals, a trap
a door is an opening into a room

explanation.surface: Drinking before a first night could make a performer fail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' is a snare, not the drink; 'let down' means lower through the stage floor, not disappoint.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged panel in a stage floor drops a performer out of sight.

clue.text: Deny a key's stupidly mislaid outside

indicators.note: outside means the jumbled letters of mislaid wrap round the key
stupidly suggests mislaid is muddled into a new order

parts.note: C is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone denies foolishly losing a key outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' makes DISLAIM from MISLAID; 'outside' puts it round C.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce or refuse to acknowledge responsibility is to repudiate.

indicators.note: lacking shows that the letter standing for nothing is dropped

parts.note: to do well is to prosper
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A blessing wishing someone long life and success, minus something.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to inhabit it.
